lead: OBD-II (on-board diagnostics, second generation) is the standard that lets one scan tool plug into any compliant car and read its emissions-related faults and live engine data. It fixes the 16-pin connector and its pins, the bus protocols, the request services, the parameter numbers and the format of the fault codes. It became law for petrol cars in the USA from 1996 and in Europe (as EOBD) from 2001; in India the BS-VI Phase 2 rules of April 2023 brought full OBD-II monitoring. A workshop uses it to find why the malfunction lamp is on, to read sensor values while the engine runs and to check that the engine computer has finished its self-tests.
prereq: You need CAN frames and the transport layer from the OSI model, and hexadecimal numbers.

sections.h3: The 16-pin connector and the bus protocols

blocks.text: Before OBD-II each maker had its own socket and its own codes. The standard connector (SAE J1962) has 16 pins in two rows of eight and must sit within reach of the driver's seat, usually under the dashboard near the steering column. The pins with fixed jobs are:

The other pins are left to the maker. Five protocols were allowed: SAE J1850 PWM, SAE J1850 VPW, ISO 9141-2, ISO 14230 (KWP2000) and ISO 15765-4 (CAN). Cars sold in the USA from model year 2008 must use CAN, and so do new cars elsewhere. On CAN, OBD-II allows 11-bit or 29-bit identifiers, each at 500 kbit/s or 250 kbit/s; most cars use 11-bit at 500 kbit/s, and 29-bit at 250 kbit/s is common on heavy vehicles. The tool takes power from pins 16 and 4 or 5, tries CAN on pins 6 and 14, and falls back to the older pins if no ECU answers.
The tool sends a request whose first byte is a service (or mode) number; the ECU answers with the service number plus 0x40. The standard services are:

head: Service
What it does
rows: Freeze frame: data stored at the moment a fault was set
Clear codes and stored test results, switch the lamp off
Oxygen sensor test results (not used on CAN cars, which use service 06)
Pending codes: faults seen in the current or last drive cycle but not yet confirmed
Control of an on-board test or component
Vehicle information, such as the VIN
Permanent codes, which a scan tool cannot clear

blocks.text: A parameter identifier (PID) names one value. The reply to service 01 is 0x41, the PID, then data bytes A, B and so on. The tool must apply the scaling for that PID:

OBD-II reaches only the emissions-related data. A workshop's own tester goes further with the maker's enhanced diagnostics, today usually UDS (unified diagnostic services, ISO 14229): read data by identifier, read trouble-code information, security access, routine control and reprogramming, for the ABS, airbag, body and every other ECU, routed through the gateway.

sections.h3: Fault codes, monitors and the lamp

blocks.text: A diagnostic trouble code (DTC) is a letter and four digits. The letter is the system: P powertrain, C chassis, B body, U network. The first digit is 0 for a generic code defined by the standard and 1 for a maker-specific one (2 and 3 are split between the two). For P codes the second digit is the subsystem (1 and 2 fuel and air metering, 3 ignition and misfire, 4 emission controls, 5 speed and idle control, 6 computer and outputs, 7 and 8 transmission), and the last two digits name the fault. P0301 is a generic misfire in cylinder 1. On the bus each DTC is two bytes: the top 2 bits give the letter (00 P, 01 C, 10 B, 11 U), the next 2 bits the first digit, and the remaining three groups of 4 bits the last three digits.

Monitors are self-tests the ECU runs: misfire, fuel system and comprehensive components run all the time; catalyst, oxygen sensor, oxygen sensor heater, evaporative system and EGR run only when their conditions are met during a drive cycle (cold start, warm-up, steady cruise, idle). The readiness status (service 01, PID 01) shows which monitors have completed since the codes were last cleared. When a monitor first fails, the ECU stores a pending code. Most faults are two-trip faults: if the same fault is found in the next drive cycle, the code is confirmed, a freeze frame is stored and the malfunction indicator lamp (MIL) comes on. A misfire bad enough to damage the catalyst lights the MIL at once, and flashes it. After three good drive cycles in a row the lamp goes off, and the code is erased after about 40 warm-up cycles without the fault. Service 04 clears codes, but a fault that is still there returns, and a permanent code stays until its monitor passes.

examples.question: A scan tool sends 01 0C (live engine speed). The ECU replies 41 0C 1A F0. Find the engine speed.
steps: The reply starts 41 (service 01 + 0x40) and 0C (the PID), so the data bytes are A = 0x1A and B = 0xF0.
Each count is 0.25 rpm, so speed = 6896 ÷ 4 = 1724 rpm.
examples.answer: The engine is running at 1724 rpm.

examples.question: Service 03 on a CAN car returns 43 02 03 01 01 33. A freeze frame for the first code gives PID 05 = 0x7B, PID 0D = 0x3E and PID 04 = 0x59. Decode the codes and the freeze frame.
steps: 43 is the reply to service 03; 02 says two codes follow; the codes are 03 01 and 01 33.
0x0301: first byte 0000 0011. Top two bits 00 → P; next two bits 00 → first digit 0; low four bits 0011 → 3; second byte 0x01 → digits 0 and 1. Code P0301, misfire in cylinder 1.
0x0133: first byte 0000 0001 → P, 0, 1; second byte 0x33 → 3 and 3. Code P0133, oxygen sensor slow response, bank 1 sensor 1.
Engine load: A = 0x59 = 89, so 89 × 100 ÷ 255 = 34.9 per cent.
examples.answer: Codes P0301 (cylinder 1 misfire) and P0133 (slow oxygen sensor, bank 1 sensor 1); the misfire was set with the engine warm at 83 °C, at 62 km/h and about 35 per cent load.

traps: The P in P0301 means powertrain, not petrol. C is chassis, B body, U network.
A generic scan tool does read P1xxx codes through service 03; what it lacks is the maker's table that says what each one means.
Pins 4 and 5 are grounds and pin 16 is battery positive; CAN is on pins 6 and 14, not 6 and 16.
A freeze frame is stored data from the moment the fault was confirmed, read with service 02; live data is service 01.
Clearing codes with service 04 switches the lamp off but does not repair the fault, and it resets the readiness monitors, so the car fails an inspection that checks them.

quiz.q: Which J1962 pins carry battery positive, the two grounds and CAN?
quiz.a: Pin 16 battery positive; pins 4 (chassis) and 5 (signal) ground; pins 6 CAN high and 14 CAN low.

quiz.q: Which services read stored, pending and permanent codes?
quiz.a: Service 03 stored (confirmed) codes, service 07 pending codes, service 0A permanent codes.

quiz.q: Explain the two-trip rule for lighting the MIL.
quiz.a: When a monitor first fails, the ECU stores only a pending code. If the same fault is found again in the next drive cycle, the code is confirmed, a freeze frame is stored and the MIL comes on. This avoids lighting the lamp for a one-off glitch.

quiz.q: PID 0C returns A = 0x0C, B = 0x80. Find the engine speed.
PID 05 returns 0x28. What is the coolant temperature, and what does it tell you?
quiz.a: 0x28 = 40, so 40 − 40 = 0 °C. The engine is stone cold (or the sensor is reading wrongly), so warm-up monitors have not run.
0x41 = 0100 0001: top bits 01 → C; next bits 00 → 0; low nibble 1 → 1; 0x23 → 2 and 3. Code C0123, a generic chassis code.

quiz.q: A driver clears the codes; the MIL goes off but returns two days later. Explain.
quiz.a: Service 04 erased the codes and the lamp, but the fault was not repaired. When the monitor ran again it failed, set a pending code, failed again on the next drive cycle, confirmed the code and lit the MIL.

quiz.q: Why can a generic OBD-II tool not read an airbag fault?
quiz.a: OBD-II covers only emissions-related systems. The airbag ECU's codes are read with the maker's enhanced diagnostics (UDS), which a generic tool does not know.

beyond: Not for the exam. The same socket now feeds fleet telematics, insurance dongles and remote diagnostics, and makers lock it with security access and secure gateways. Diagnostics over IP (DoIP) uses Ethernet for fast flashing, and newer rules move toward remote, over-the-air emissions monitoring. Search for SAE J1979, ISO 14229 UDS, DoIP and readiness monitors.
